clue.text: "Man seeketh in society comfort, use and ______" (Bacon)

definitions.text: "Man seeketh in society comfort, use and ______" (Bacon)

parts.words: "Man seeketh in society comfort, use and ______" (Bacon)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Francis Bacon's essay Of Friendship: the solver supplies the missing final noun, the shelter that company gives

explanation.surface: A line of Francis Bacon's on why people seek company, with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation clue rather than wordplay: Bacon wrote that man seeks in society comfort, use and the safety others give.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Bacon's list of what company offers: safety and shelter from harm.

clue.text: Object to being ordered to go again

explanation.surface: Someone bristles at being told to set off once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SENT, the second reading is 'sent again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to take offence at it; split with a hyphen, the word means dispatched a second time.

clue.text: A beastly fighter will have to 21 alternatively

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 21 across, meaning learn
alternatively means or, offering another choice

explanation.surface: A bullfighter must be studied, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer of 21 across, READ.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador fights bulls in the ring, so his opponent is a beast.

clue.text: May this lead to imprisonment for one's strongly-held opinion?

explanation.surface: Could someone be jailed for their firmly held beliefs?
explanation.definitionFit: A guilty verdict in court can send someone to prison, and the same word means a firm belief.

clue.text: Unusually nice lad from the country

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of nice lad come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rather odd young man who comes from somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges NICE LAD; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Some soprano valiantly striving to become a new star

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer bravely strives for stardom.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'striving to become a new star' as the definition, but that phrase cannot stand for a noun; 'a new star' is the definition and 'striving to become' only links. The run spans sopraNO VAliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for new, a nova is a star that flares suddenly, once thought to be newly born.

clue.text: Prefer sage, just the same

parts.note: to prefer something is to like it
a sage person is wise

explanation.surface: Someone chooses the herb sage, and the next person says me too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' reads as the herb but is the adjective wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in the same way, also, as when agreeing with someone.

clue.text: Restored control and reported

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, hence control
reported means stated, said

explanation.surface: Order was brought back and the news put out.
explanation.definitionFit: Put back into a former position, as an official returned to office.

clue.text: Firm base?

parts.note: read firm as a noun, a company, and ask where such a business is based and its staff work

explanation.surface: A request for solid foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective, solid, but is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's workplace is where its business is run from day to day.

clue.text: Set against the new sergeant

indicators.note: new says the letters of sergeant are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly arrived sergeant is regarded with hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SERGEANT; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to make them hostile to each other.

clue.text: Get to know about article made of hide

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around another

parts.note: to get to know something is to learn it
the is the definite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Learning about something fashioned from animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is a grammar term here, the definite article; 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective for things fashioned from tanned animal skin.

clue.text: Bookwork almost finished the boss!

indicators.note: almost finished means stop just short of the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: bookwork is study, reading and learning

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's reading nearly done, to the head's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' drops the last letter of STUDY. A boss here is a raised knob or ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised knob, the same as an ornamental nail head.

clue.text: An entertainer's exposure

parts.note: read exposure literally as baring the body, the act of a performer who removes clothes slowly on stage

explanation.surface: A performer's publicity or media coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposure' suggests publicity, but means undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque act in which a performer gradually undresses to music.

clue.text: Cannot stir when engaged in a confinement

indicators.note: engaged means locked together like gears, so the letters of the two words are meshed into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner unable to move while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' mixes CANNOT and STIR into one rearrangement. 'stir' looks like the anagram signal or prison slang, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint or restriction that holds something in check.

clue.text: Writers, these — and not bad — about public transport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled words go around the next piece
bad says the letters of these and not are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway

explanation.surface: Authors who are not bad, discussed on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' is the anagram signal, giving THEONTES before 'about' wraps it round the railway. BR is British Rail, the UK's former state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were English novelist sisters of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Don't have an arbitrator come down

parts.note: a ref, or referee, arbitrates in a game
to rain is to come down from the sky

explanation.surface: Decline to hire a referee who might then get wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain from something is to choose not to take it.

clue.text: To proceed with so much hesitation would be a bloomer

parts.note: to flow is to proceed smoothly

indicators.note: so much here means a repeated amount, the sound appearing twice over

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Stumbling along with so many pauses would be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so much' doubles ER. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blossoms; a bloomer flowers in its season.

clue.text: A course to run without point

indicators.note: without means outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to desert is to run away
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A race route that goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense means outside: DESERT goes round S.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet dish served at the end of a meal is one of its stages.

clue.text: Suppress the Left in odd situation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one letter goes into the word for odd

parts.note: an odd situation is a strange one

explanation.surface: Silencing the political left in an unusual set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke back or stifle, as one might a yawn or a protest.

clue.text: Issue Number 1 with current back-up

indicators.note: in a down clue back-up means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the figure 1 is I in Roman numerals
a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: The first issue of a publication, with spare copies in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' turns NO + I + TIDE upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single printing of a magazine or newspaper is one issue.

clue.text: Walker's people in for a radical set-back

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: set-back says the word for radical is set backwards

parts.note: a red is a political radical
men are people

explanation.surface: Supporters of a stroller rally behind a leftist who has suffered a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' turns RED to DER; 'in' puts MEN inside PRO + A + DER. 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strolling along a seafront, or a concertgoer standing at the Proms.

clue.text: Some soldiers take little notice but learn

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
an ad is a small advertisement or notice

explanation.surface: Troops pay scant attention yet still pick things up.
explanation.walkthrough: RE = Royal Engineers; 'take' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a text is to learn it, as in reading law at university.

clue.text: A colourless individual

parts.note: read colourless literally, a person lacking pigment in skin and hair, rather than a dull character

explanation.surface: A dull, boring person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colourless' suggests dull, but means without pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born without melanin has white hair and pale skin.

clue.text: Men rowing about agreement's sense

indicators.note: about means around, so the crew goes around the word of agreement

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Oarsmen arguing over the meaning of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rowing' looks like quarrelling but is the sport; an eight is a rowing crew. 'about' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Take a breath and talk over parking

indicators.note: over means placed above, as in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly, chatter
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone pauses for air while chatting about where to leave the car.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw in air sharply, a short inhalation.

clue.text: A toiling eccentric's artistic work

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of a toiling are set out in an odd order; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A hard-working oddball's art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric's' rearranges A TOILING.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraved or incised design, cut into a gem or metal surface.

clue.text: Ship carrying a great many pieces of pottery

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: SS is steamship
a herd is a great many, a large crowd

explanation.surface: A vessel laden with lots of crockery fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the containment signal; SS is a standard prefix for a steamship's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of shards, broken fragments found by archaeologists.

clue.text: Shut up and check on this 16 down!

parts.note: pent means shut up, confined, as in pent-up
to stem is to check or stop a flow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A command to be quiet and keep an eye on a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: '16 down' points to FLOWERER, so the definition is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Beardtongue is a garden plant of the figwort family with tubular blossoms.
